discoveryRecommendations: Search the complete officially profiled inventory using the full broad interest pattern first. The 12 fields are navigational, overlapping tags, not closed eligibility boundaries.

Do not require novices to recognize/affirm every profession's functions before a strong match. Use converging broad-interest evidence and valid task analogues; preserve uncertainty and genuine domain conflicts.
Keep interest strength, preparation, experience, conditions and affordability separate. Degree willingness and high income cannot generate interest support.
Import current official whole interest profiles and where available specific interest areas; do not convert authored tags into claimed aptitude scores.
Prevent synonym/industry/subtype inflation and multiple counting of the same evidence. New SOC alone does not guarantee new coverage.
Use task descriptions in explanations and optional later exploration, explicitly not a replacement profession-by-profession question bank.
implementationCautions: Priority means distinct useful breadth, not guaranteed matches or mandatory launch order.
Only activate with verified codes, official interest data, scope/route mapping and first-paid-stage budgets. O*NET partial profiles remain explicit gaps.
Network/database architecture, editing and curriculum roles carry experience concerns. Do not treat inventory inclusion as direct post-degree readiness.
Health information and music have mixed routes; do not inflate bachelor-required inventory by relabeling aggregates.
Small research occupations can fit while having few openings; market demand and starting compensation remain separate.
Evaluate precision and recall on unseen profiles; larger catalog must not turn each weak neighbor into a strong match.
